utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, there are something like five applications made which have to be disposed of, and I'm afraid you're going to have to explain to me what you mean by the proposition put forward by the Defence that they can prove that the Muslims were attacking the Serbs. When would be the best time to deal with those?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps after this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps after this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right then. We'll proceed with this witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, we finished last week with you describing the circumstances under which you showed photo arrays to witnesses VG87 and VG78?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention -- did there come a time when you showed a photo array to a witness with the pseudonym VG101?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown Exhibit 55-VG101. It's here. May I note for the Court, over the weekend, Your Honour, we have reorganised your binder so these exhibits are in your binder now under tab 55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, is that the photo array that you showed witness VG101?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I showed this photo array on the 21st of March 2001, this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that is the original array that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There is absolutely no challenge to that fact. Why do we have to get every witness to refer to every fact when there's no challenge to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm trying to establish foundation for the entry of that piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Why wasn't it tendered at the time? I asked you at the time and you said you wanted to wait for him. Why? There is no challenge to it. Let's get things in as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can explain what I'm proposing to the Court. After I laid a foundation I have colour photocopies. I've an agreement from Mr. Domazet that they will be tendered at the same time and under no objection into evidence so that the original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good. Let's get on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you showed a photo array to Witness 105?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 55-VG105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can't you show them to him all at once?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's only one more, Your Honour. If you'd like I'll send them up at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If there is one thing that wastes time is doing this sort of thing

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the one that I showed to witness 105 on the 23rd of March of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For two witnesses was there a different procedure followed?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason for this different procedure followed was that we ran out of arrays. We didn't have enough. So the procedure was that the witnesses had a look at the array, pointed out the person if they knew -- recognised any person, pointed out the person and then signed the array on the rear side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was their section then noted in their statement?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was such a procedure followed with witnesses VG13 and VG59?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 55-VG13.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photo spread I showed to the witnesses on -- on the 21st of July, 2000, and also on the 13th of May, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I move or tender the following documents all Exhibit -- all number 55, but with the suffix VG87, VG78, VG101, VG105, and VG13. I would tender at this time colour photocopies of those exhibits into evidence and I have an agreement from Mr. Domazet that the colour copies will suffice in lieu of the originals. I have the originals in court should the Court itself wish to examine the original documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And that's by consent, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. They will be Exhibits 55 with those suffixes, 87, 78, 101, 105, and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, did there come a time when you went to Visegrad to view medical records in connection with this case?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Chamber when you did that?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that on the 1st of November, 2000, together with Investigator Ewa, with Senior Trial Attorney Joanne Korner, and the interpreter and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who were you there in Visegrad to see regarding these medical records?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to see, first of all, Mr. Domazet and also Dr. Moljevic who was supposed to arrive in Visegrad from Uzice

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you in fact meet with Dr. Moljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he in fact show you records which he represented to be the medical records concerning Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you also have in your possession at that time a court order authorising you to seize those records?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had with us a court order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you in fact seize those records?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We seized the records on the 1st of November, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd ask that the witness be shown this large blue ledger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, do you recognise that large blue ledger?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of two ledgers seized on the 1st of November, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take a look at the -- there's a photocopy inside that -- the cover of that ledger. That is Exhibit number 13 -- or number -- Prosecution number 136. Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the page on -- at the top of this page, number 1014, is the name of the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic, written in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you yourself make a photocopy of that page from that large blue ledger?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you be able to find the original page should the Court care to look at it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think we need to look at that time, but there is, I think, some importance in what was the last -- the heading on the last column, which is a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll be introducing an official translation of all these documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. But we've only ever been shown a photostat with the entry relating to Mr. Vasiljevic, which does not include the headings, and whereas we can guess with most of them, the one with the time at the end of them may or may not be important but I think we should know what is the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, did you photocopy the entire page on which this name appears?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Including any headings that were on the top of that page?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the ledger, it's on the front page of the ledger. It's written the year 1992, and it's an alphabetical system in Cyrillic, which I don't read. So with the help from our language assistant at the team, we found under V, Mr. Vasiljevic's name, and the date of 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Was there also another ledger that you seized on that day?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a second ledger, also a blue ledger but a thin one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown this thin blue ledger and inside the front cover is a photocopy entitled Exhibit number 137.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise that blue ledger, that thin blue ledger?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a thin blue ledger. Everything is in handwriting in it, and it was one of those two that we seized on the 1st of November, 2000. On the front page is written in Cyrillic -- I don't remember exactly the text, but it's something with patients admitted from the battlefield. And there's a date on the front page, 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to take a look at the Exhibit number or Prosecution document number 137 on the inside cover. It's a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that the accused is having some problems with his earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you able to hear the proceedings now, Mr. Vasiljevic? Can you hear the proceedings now? Yes. Yes. You proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take a look at Prosecution document number 137. Is that the photocopy you made of the pertinent page inside that thin blue ledger?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it contain the name of the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As number 188 is written in Latin the date the 14th of June, 1992, and then 2135. I think it's the time for the admission. And then Vasiljevic, Mitar, and in the column with the when and where born is written 1954, Visegrad. And then there's a diagnosis and information about who brought him to the hospital, also, from where he came. He came from the TO Visegrad, which means Territorial Defence, Visegrad. And the last column is who was informed about him being at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And who was informed him about being at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: SUP, which means the police. And then the military police, and then there's three digits, 985, which might be a military post number, but we're not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you also at this time seize a four-part document entitled medical history?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you that you be shown a four-part document as well as a photocopy entitled Prosecution document number 138 and ask you, do you recognise what that is? Do you recognise that document, the original document?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what do you recognise that to be?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a history of -- let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You can take it out of the sleeve if you want to take a closer look?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a document in which was written what happened during Mr. Vasiljevic's stay at the hospital, his treatment and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And document number 138, is that a photocopy of the original?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender Exhibits number 136, 137, and 138, photocopies of the original medical records into evidence and would make the originals available to the Chamber at this time if the Chamber would like to see the originals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When I was dealing with those orders, I was informed that the bluebook, I was told that one of them, when produced by the doctor, was covered with several years worth of dust. I think, if I may say so, that is a relevant matter which you should bring into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that was hyperbole or actual fact, but I will ask the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, can you describe the condition of the book now as opposed to the condition of the book when you first took it into custody? Are there differences between the condition of the book?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The smell, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was obvious to me that those documents had been stored for quite a long time in a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And in an undisturbed state; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to say that, by think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any dust on the books that you recall?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were dirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you submitted these books to the Dutch forensic laboratory?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from the time that you submitted those to the Dutch forensic laboratory, was there any time that they were out of the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were held in a safe, a locked safe in our team area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we better deal with them not one by one but lot by lot. You've tendered 136, 137 and 138, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. They will be Exhibits P136, 137, and 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does the Court wish to see the originals at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I will let you know if we need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In addition to these three -- these two ledgers and the medical form, were there other records that were seized at that time?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were in total 12 different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after you seized these documents, did you make a list of the documents that you seized or items that you seized?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made the list the day we seized the documents, and Dr. Moljevic got a copy of that list. He didn't want to sign the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to describe for the Court the other records that you seized on that day?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also seized an X-ray of a leg. The X-ray was marked Milan -- Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did it have a date on the X-ray?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 14th of June, 1992. And there were some lab statements and some blood type forms filled out from the general hospital in Uzice, and they were dated 15th of June. Then there were six temperature lists from the orthopaedic -- the first date visible on this was the 14th of June, 1992. Then there was a release list regarding a repeated fracture, which was dated on the 6th of May, 1993. And there was also a release list dated 28th of July, 1992, from the psychiatric ward at Uzice hospital. Then there were three Yellow Pages with -- they were -- the header was therapy list, and there was a history of disease from Uzice hospital, orthopaedic department, dated 14th of June, 1992. Then there was a letter in handwriting. It was signed Mitar Vasiljevic, and it was for a certain Dr. Slavica. It was dated on the 13th of July, 1992. And then we got a sample, a form like this one but.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you referring to Prosecution Exhibit number 138?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this form was a similar form but used nowadays, in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few questions about the X-rays separately, but other records that you refer to, are they still all in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are all held in this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And available for the Chamber should they wish to them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You did promise us an English translation, Mr Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm having draft ones converted now into official translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask you now a couple of specific questions about the X-ray. Can you describe the approximately size of this X-ray?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's the size 25 times 40 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you indicated that it had the name of the accused along the bottom of this X-ray?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did it also have a date on it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the date that was on the X-ray?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you or is the Office of the Prosecutor in possession of that X-ray today?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who is in possession of that X-ray?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A specialist, Dr. Ivan de Grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he given that by the Office of the Prosecutor to conduct some tests?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown -- brought the following four exhibits, Exhibit 17-1, 17-11, 17-12 and 17-13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, I draw your attention to Prosecution document number 17-1. Do you recognise what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The photograph is actually two that are put together, and those two photographs show Visegrad. It's aerial photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prosecution document number 17-11, can you describe what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the front of hotel Visegrad in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Prosecution document number 17-12, can you tell us what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is restaurant Panos at the main gate in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally Prosecution number 17-13. Can you tell us, do you recognise what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also restaurant Panos in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do all of these photographs accurately depict the sites that they are -- are contained in these photographs, fairly and accurately depict those sites?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's one thing with the area photo showing Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's exhibit -- that's Prosecution document number 17-1?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe what it is about that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it's two aerial photos put together, it might show where they're covering each other, the same house two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that that -- 17-1 be placed on the ELMO so Investigator Hansen can indicate the portion of the photograph he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to indicate the portion of the photograph which may have some of the houses repeated in it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, answer -- exactly where they are put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from that, does it fairly and accurately depict the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this year, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender Prosecution document number 17-1, 17-11, 17-12 and 17-13 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't have my microphone on. I will repeat that. They will be Exhibits P17.1, 17.11, 17.12 and 17.13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions of Investigator Hansen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hansen, you said in your answers that some of the evidence that you recognised today in exhibits were the subject of special analysis by the Forensic Institute in Holland, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, which of these documents were the subject of that expertise?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a typewritten document that we sent for further examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the two blue ledgers, the large blue ledger, 1992, and the smaller blue book with the date of admittance into evidence as being the 14th of June, 1992? Were they the subject of expert analysis too?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I'm correct, I think on the 25th of June this year, when photographs were taken of several important locations in Visegrad which are relevant to this case, you were there. You were on the spot; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but to me it sounds correct. It was at the end of June, that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You visited the house in Pionirska Street and the premises in which the witnesses say they were shut in and burnt; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We visited the house near the creek in Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you perhaps note down the dimensions of the room in which the people were detained when the place was set fire to, the dimensions of the room? Do you have them?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you measure the dimensions of the house, that house in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time you visited the house and examined it, were there any windows in the room facing the creek?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, you mean window frames left or just openings?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Window frames, because we can clearly see on the photograph that there are two apertures, two openings, but we can't see whether the openings have the window frames or whether windows existed at all?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the photo with me. As far as I remember, there were burnt wood in some of the window openings, and there were -- there was also burnt timber in the rooms, or half -- partly burnt timber. And there was a door in the basement with a padlock on. What was behind that door, we don't know. But this door was a new one. It wasn't a door that had ever been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You were talking about the door to that particular room on the ground floor basement, the room that the witnesses say they were locked up in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the witnesses have told in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I wasn't thinking of their testimony in court. I was thinking of what they perhaps indicated on the spot, in view of the fact that, at that time, they were together with you, as far as I know from the material that I received.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't next to the witnesses all the time, so I'm not, I think, the right person to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One more question in this connection. I didn't quite follow you. Did you look at the room, the premises that we're talking about? Did you open the door and have a look inside? You said you didn't measure the room, but I'm interested in knowing whether you took a look, whether you looked to see what it was like on the inside.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I looked from outside into that room, through the window openings, and I saw this door, this wooden door inside the room, from the first room to another one; and what was behind this locked door, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. That same day, you were at the Vilina Vlas hotel. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the reception area of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at the reception area in the hotel on this morning in late June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, what the size of the reception area is, or, rather, how far it is from the entrance to the hotel to the actual reception desk; can you tell me that? In your assessment, how far would that be, the entrance to the reception desk?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say ten metres, 10 to 12 metres from the glass door to the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. And now a few questions with respect to the photograph albums or arrays that you showed the witnesses. The photograph of Mitar Vasiljevic is the photograph that was taken after his arrest here in The Hague; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you have a photograph of him from that period, that is to say, dating back to 1992? And if so, why didn't you use that photograph for the photo array?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have a photo of the accused taken back in 1992. I remember having seen one in a newspaper, a Bosnian newspaper at a certain stage. I don't remember the date or when, but definitely after his address, because as far as I understood, his arrest was mentioned in an article in the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Not only in one. There were several articles that came out in the Bosnian Federation with Mitar Vasiljevic's photograph in them, but they all date to the period after the arrest. That is to say, the photographs are from here. And that's why I asked my question, because I assumed that many witnesses were able to see the photographs before you showed them, in view of the fact that a year went by since Vasiljevic was first arrested. That's why I asked you. So you didn't have a photograph of him dating back to the earlier period. Now, if it's no secret, can you tell us whether on the other photographs in the photo array, whether there were any other suspects or were there any other people from Visegrad or were the others people at random who have nothing to do with Visegrad at all?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo arrays were mixed. We used several different arrays, and I remember at a certain stage we used a black and white photo array that also included photos of other persons from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Therefore, if I understand you correctly, there were photographs of people from Visegrad amongst them, too, but not any of the direct suspects relating to this case; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photo array in black and white, there were the -- the black and white photo of the accused plus photos of other persons from Visegrad. We also had a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look. You really must answer the question. He's asking whether they are suspects, not just whether they're from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were persons involved in what happened in Visegrad in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are they suspects?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's only in the black and white photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that answer your question, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would just like to know directly whether there were Sredoje Lukic's and Milan Lukic's photographs amongst the photo array.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On very few occasions, yes. I think we have showed the photo array with Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic just two times or so. But I'm not sure, I didn't count.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought that you had told us on Thursday that you used the same photographs but in a different order. Was that just in relation to the colour photographs, was it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the black and white ones, we have some black and white ones in evidence, have we? I haven't seen them yet.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the black and white photos were shown to people that are not called to give testimony during this -- no ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure why they've been tendered then. Why are the black and white ones being tendered, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the ones that you have in your hand --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The exhibits you have in your hand have been shown to witnesses. The investigator is talking about other photographs, which I believe I can clear up with a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: These are black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we better get this very clear because the point that Mr. Domazet makes may turn out to be an important one as to the validity of this photograph identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I suggest you better try and explore it in re-examination, because the point has been fair and squarely raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, were you responsible for investigating a number of different crimes that occurred in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you refer to Mr. Domazet's question regarding suspects, that their photographs were contained in those photo arrays, did you mean people in addition to Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and the accused?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were they in connection with other crimes that occurred in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, we've entered in a number of photographs this morning, photo arrays that were shown to VG87, VG78, VG101, and VG105.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Mr. Groome, they, of course, have their full signatures on the back. Those documents better be under seal, had they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry, I did mean to tender them under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that relate to all of those --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, all of the photo arrays --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All the ones with 17 as a prefix.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, 17 are photographs, Your Honour, these are all 55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 55. Very well. All of those commencing with the numbers 55 will be under seal. Now, the other point, now that I've seen the documents, I have absolutely no idea which one of the witnesses on the front -- I'm sorry, which one the photographs on the front has been identified by these people. Is the positioning of the signature on the back intended to suggest that they have identified different people or in each case have they identified the photograph which happens to be of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you putting that to the witness or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, I'll clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the sort of thing that we just see it for the first time now, it doesn't make it at all clear what that document's intended to mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, let me just finish up my question to you. The witness -- the photo arrays that were shown to Witness number 87, 78, 101, and 105, those photo arrays, did they contain the picture of any other person, any other suspect in Visegrad or of the two other accused in this case, Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic? If you need to see them again --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, they are now formally in evidence. I don't know the procedure in your court, whether you will use the Court's -- the actual exhibit or a copy that I have.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I don't have any extra copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we'll use your copies. We're not going to give up your copies, frankly. And the Court Deputy makes a very good point. There should be one that is the actual exhibit not just the three copies that are for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was the one that I just tendered a few minutes ago, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's why I tendered the colour copies in lieu of the originals?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm still at a complete loss to know what you are doing, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: A complete loss. Now is the original of these documents we've got in colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Why have we got black and white ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have colour copies except for this one, Your Honour, because it was impossible -- the colour copy machine was unavailable at the time and we needed to make copies over the weekend. You have colour copies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I suggest that you take them back and get them colour copied so we do have a copy of the exhibit, otherwise we will wonder what on earth this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But that probably cures the problem with this document, which is now Exhibit 55VG13, but it still doesn't make clear which of those photographs the people who signed it on the back identified them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With a few questions I think I can clear this up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at the end of the portion of your testimony where you described a different procedure being shown, I believe that you testified to the Court that did you not have sufficient photo arrays to show all the witnesses that you wanted to show photographs to?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, had one witness signed a photograph would you have been able to use that with a subsequent witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Because you were out of the country at the time, what procedure did you or what adaptation did you make to your procedure in order to ensure the fairness of this photo array?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had ten pictures of ten different men, one of them were or is the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic, and we numbered the pictures from 1 to 10, and at the end of the witness -- no, no, statement, we asked or I asked if it was possible for the witness or if the witness thought he would be able to recognise the said person, Mitar Vasiljevic. Then I showed them those ten pictures, asking them to point out if they knew or recognised any of those ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did you document the choice that each witness made?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was written in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that statement then read back to the witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was read back to the witness and it was signed by the witness, by myself, and by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And -- on -- sorry. Continue.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to this, I asked the witness to sign on the rear side of the photo space.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And their signature on the rear side, does it indicate anything other than the fact that they had an opportunity to see these photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The positioning of the signatures has no bearing to the photographs on the front; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the signatures are spread out obviously across the back of the colour photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the positioning of the signatures has no bearing as to the photograph which they say they recognised Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those I know, one of the witnesses that signed on the rear side, didn't recognise anybody from those ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it indicates that the witness has seen this photo spread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, can I get an answer to my question? I'm sorry to be persistent, but I think we have to have it. The positioning of the signatures on the back of that sheet has no bearing upon the particular photograph which they identified as that of Mr. Vasiljevic and indeed one of them didn't identify anybody as Mr. Vasiljevic? You seem to be at a loss. You see, in all of the other documents we've seen, somebody has signed the particular photograph that they identified --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- which is the usual way with a photographic identification, so that there is an indisputable piece of evidence and that is the particular photograph they identified, a very wise way of doing it. Now, this time, you couldn't do it because you say you didn't have enough copies of the colour document, but there is nothing on the photograph now or the signatures on the back which demonstrates that they identified any particular photograph on the front it as that of Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If we want to know if any of the persons that signed on the rear side recognised any of the persons shown on the photos, one has to read the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: With all the problems of Prosecution statements being translated twice. But anyway, this document doesn't assist us on that issue. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, would it be fire say that the signatures on the back were simply done just in the order that the people had the opportunity to see the photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, were any of these witnesses shown these photographs in the company of other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were myself, the interpreter and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the original of VG or 55-VG13, the original of that document, is it a colour reproduced set of photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The original of the document that the Judge has just referred to, you just had it in your hand moment ago, is that a -- was the original of that a colour document just like the other coloured photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a coloured photo spread, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And speaking about this particular array of 55-VG13, was -- did it contain the photograph of any other suspects or of Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It contain the photograph of Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Mr. Domazet asked you a couple of questions regarding windows in the house. I'm going to ask you to look at my copy of Exhibit 17-10. I'm going to ask that that be placed on the ELMO for the witness. Investigator Hansen, I'm going to ask you to take the pointer and ask you to indicate by holding the pointer still where precisely the creek would be in relation to this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you just to hold it still just for a second there?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there's a person who seems to be standing by two openings in the wall. Did they appear to you be windows, those openings in the wall?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to characterise those windows as facing the creek?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were those windows on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on the ground floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you describe in response to Mr. Domazet's questions, a door that was locked. Can you please put the pointer and hold it there for a few seconds to indicate where that door was?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was there any other way to -- were you able to access through the inside of this premises at any time during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no windows to that room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is the door something that you can see in the photograph, those two vertical lines? Are those the edges of the door?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to trace the outline of the door with the pointer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can only say, Mr. Groome, to have to go back and look at the video of this particular piece of evidence later to see what he's pointing at is a pretty horrific task.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's also a better copy in your binders now if you care to look at the original copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You've made no attempt, if I may say so, to get on to the transcript precisely where he is pointing. Yes. The photograph that I've been shown certainly does show a door. And it's not where the man standing but around the corner from it facing the photographer. Is that a fair description of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask, Investigator Hansen, if you'd take the black pen in front of you and if you could just write the word "door" across the door on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My only concern with this Your Honours, is I'm working with a copy, not the one that was entered into evidence so this isn't preserved for the record properly either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we can substitute one or the other if it's as good a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is the exact same copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I ask you to write the word "window" and just draw an arrow to indicate where the windows were.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Investigator Hansen, you also described seeing some type of wooden structure contained in this building. Can you indicate on this photograph where approximately that structure would be?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the top floor and on the -- what is -- if this is the ground floor, then I'll call this -- oh, sorry. I'll call this floor the first floor and this the second floor. And there was a partly burned structure on the second floor and also some on the first floor, and a lot of rubbish all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What you're describing now is the ground floor. Aside from these two windows facing the creek, were there any windows facing the Pionirska Street on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground floor, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any windows facing where the photographer would have been to take this picture?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was one, but -- yes, there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll substitute, if we can, the document which is presently the exhibit for the one the witness has been writing on. We'll give you back the one that was the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I please make a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we possibly just add a suffix to this with the investigator's name? There may be other witnesses that I would ask to look at this photograph and I wouldn't want to influence their testimony by seeing Mr. Hansen's marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. What was the number of this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So that's 17.10. Maybe we put could Hansen after it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we'll put 17.10-1 for the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the one he's marked and that will be the one we'll call the Hansen document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, when that's been done, it can be shown to Mr. Domazet. Well, thank you, sir for coming along to give evidence. You can -- yes, Mr. Domazet. What do you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I, in connection with Mr. Groome's question, ask an additional question of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Why -- Mr. Domazet --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with this explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You raised the issue. You didn't ask him for the explanation. You left it up in the air and that gives Mr. Groome the entitlement to have it explained but you have cross-examined. You've had your chance. Why should you now have another one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's merely a matter of the witness's explanation when he was pointing to the creek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no. Look, Mr. Domazet, there is a very clear procedure. You get your opportunity, you raise the issue, you can ask him to explain, and you can cross-examine him on his explanation, but you can't come back another time because you don't like an answer that he's given in re-examination. Re-examination is the end of the evidence. If, of course, the Prosecution had raised some new matter, you would have had the right to cross-examine upon that, because they could have raised new matter only by leave. But it's not new matter. It's dealing with the issue you raised in cross-examination. Now, if you can suggest to me somehow that this is new, you can try, but I think you may have some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not cross-examine regarding the position of the creek. Mr. Groome or, rather, the witness 1 showed on the photograph where the creek was. My question is that the creek is on the side shown by the witness, but my question would be to show whether the creek followed the length of the building or the position of the creek in relation to the house, nothing more. Maybe it's not all that important, since there is more evidence along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No. I am happy to concede, I'm just looking through the evidence. I'm happy to concede that I do not think there was any reference to the creek in the course of the cross-examination. So on that basis, you may ask any questions you may wish about the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My question for the witness is: The creek that you showed on this photograph, in what direction does to flow? Does it follow the direction -- is it parallel to the wall of the building with the windows on it? That is, is it on this side of the building?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not completely parallel to the building. It's -- it's -- it flows from the top of the picture to the bottom, and there's a bank or I would say three metres from where the person is seen on the photo to the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Just one more question. Is there any kind of inclination or a slope between the house and the creek? Is there an angle?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a slope, a very steep one. I would say two or three metres. It begins two or three metres to the left from the wall with the window openings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any re-examination arising out of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, sir, I was about to say you can go back to work. Thank you for coming along.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well now, Mr. Groome, we'll deal with these matters that you've raised in this confetti of paper that we've received over the last few days. The applications for video-conference testimony. There's one for VG105, one for VG87. Have you got anything to say about those, Mr. Domazet? VG105 is the one who has received a recommendation from her doctor that she should not travel, and the assessment by the deponent that she is frail in health. Do you object to a video-conference evidence there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In this case, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What about VG87? That's the one with the bad heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Because I received one document this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Join the club.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, VG87.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I just received this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if you'd like a chance to read it, you may certainly have it, but it's a medical issue again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. If it's a health problem, I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, then, we'll make orders. You will have to organise a date, Mr. Groome, so that a formal order can be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had left a message with one of your legal officers proposing a week from this coming Thursday as the date that we do all of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I have a message to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if that's acceptable to the Court I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the problem, as I understand it, it takes a little longer than that for it to be organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We have it organised for that day for some of the witnesses that we applied for videolink testimony several weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It's the same day, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We'll try to do it the same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And will we get through them all in a day?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If not, we have arrangements for the morning of the Friday that following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right then. Well, we'll get orders, formal orders written up because the audio-visual people, for good reason, like to have them. They like to have something in writing anyway. So we'll have those orders made in relation to those two witnesses and for them to give evidence on the 27th and/or the 28th. Now, Mr. Groome, the next thing, I'm trying to keep them in chronological order, is your response to the Defence's explanation for calling all this evidence about the Muslims attacking the Serbs. I'm not sure quite what it is you are saying. You seem to be saying - I may be wrong - that it is irrelevant, but it is nevertheless, admissible in order to give a more balanced view of the context. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this past year I've had -- worked very much in Serbia. I know Mr. Domazet's reputation as an attorney there. I guess I'm reluctant at this stage to try to curtail his ability to try his case as he sees fit. I would probably -- I would not object if Mr. Domazet introduces some evidence that he thinks gives the Court a more balanced perception of what occurred in the spring of 1992 to balance some of the witnesses that the Prosecution called. I would object to any arguments being made that somehow attacks against Serbs somehow justified the crimes in this case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Or are in any other way relevant. You see, this is what I want to know. If it is irrelevant, we will make no findings about it. You see, I hope that nobody will take offence if I put it this way, but this is an issue upon which both parties are really not facing up to what we have to determine. This is the third case that I have been in where there have been Serb -- has been a Serbian accused or a Bosnian Serb accused in which the case relates to attacks upon the Muslim civilian population. In each case, this is an issue which is put forward. I rather think, as I say, I don't want to be offensive, but it's put forward for some political agenda, because we -- if it's irrelevant, we will make no findings on it, none at all. So the evidence just sits there. If there is some relevance, I have yet to be persuaded by anybody what the relevance is. Nobody has been able to even come close to providing any explanation, let alone an acceptable one, as to why it's relevant. Now, the Prosecution, on the other hand, has its own political agenda, and again I'm not trying to be offensive, but this is what it appears to be: It wants to keep its position open so that it can introduce a whole lot of material called "background material" which is also equally irrelevant. Now, somebody, sometime, somehow has got to face up to this. I had hoped that we might get some sort of official Prosecution statement, but we haven't. We've got a statement that, frankly, means nothing. Now, are you going to permit Mr. Domazet to lead evidence of all 18 incidents that he's set out in his pre-trial defence brief?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just explain. What I am saying is it seems that Mr. Domazet is entitled to contest some of the facts that the Prosecution has alleged through their witnesses. For example, that the mortar attacks really weren't what the witness said the mortar attacks were. So I'm not objecting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But what do you suggest, that he is going to lead evidence to suggest that they were not mortar attacks? You mean, for the purposes, in relation to the purpose of the mortar attacks?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Or that there was no conflict at all in Visegrad at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought there was an admission about that, that there was an armed conflict. We still haven't got the signed documents yet, but on the draft, at least, there is an admission that there was an armed conflict at the relevant time. But I don't see that attacks by Muslims upon the Serb population in any way denies that or is at all relevant to it. An armed conflict means a conflict between two armed bodies, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct. Your Honour. I think the Prosecution also has the burden of showing that the crimes committed in this case are connected to that conflict and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How does the fact that the Serbs were being attacked by the Muslims the, the Serb civilian population was attacked by the Muslims, how is that relevant to anything that you have to prove?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's not Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the whole problem, you see. Now, I too do not want to deny Mr. Domazet the opportunity of fairly presenting his case, but I know what will happen is there will be -- whoever loses will appeal and that will become some issue in the appeal, and it's something which I think that a Trial Chamber has the obligation to avoid. So if we accept the joint approach of the parties, first of all, you may be assured, both of you, there will be no findings by the Trial Chamber, none at all. In fact, the Trial Chamber will make it abundantly clear in its judgement that such evidence as was given was given by consent and with the agreed -- and with the agreement that it was irrelevant to any issue we had to determine. So I don't know where any of these political objectives, and I'm using "political" in a very general sense, whether these political objectives will be achieved. But I am still concerned that you say some background material or some background evidence should be admitted, but you justifiably say not 18 incidents. So what happens? Does he lead evidence of one or two or 17 or 18? That's why I'm suggesting, I don't really get any assistance out of what you've put.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- I find myself in a difficult position to predict to what the evidence will appear that's why I reserve my objection to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There are 18 incidents -- I think it's 18, in the pre-trial brief by the Defence. Quite specific incidents. It will be worthy of a Prosecution's indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I simply reserved the Prosecution's right to object should it become cumulative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What does that mean? That's another word I wanted to ask you about. What do you mean when you say you don't want the evidence to become cumulative? Cumulative means they have some additional effect by their multiplication, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm using cumulative in the sense, Your Honour, that if Mr. Domazet leads such evidence at some point, it may be clear that the Chamber is now in possession of sufficient evidence on this point and to include additional evidence would be cumulative. It would be unnecessary. That could happen after testimony about the second -- two of these incidents. It could happen after five. I hardly think it would happen much more than that and that's why I reserved the Prosecution's ability to object to -- should a point come in time when that evidence would be cumulative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The point I'm making is that even the first is unnecessary, so how can we have a rule on your objection that something has suddenly become unnecessary when it's all been unnecessary? This is what, unfortunately, nobody ever seems to think about. But I have been a Trial Judge for a very long time, and this is the sort of issue that has to be determined at some stage in the trial, otherwise it gets out of hand. How can I stop Mr. Domazet, after the second one, and say, anything more is unnecessary when what he has already put is unnecessary and the Prosecution has consented to it? You're really asking the Trial Chamber to determine what's fair on a sort of an informal basis and that's not a Trial Chamber's job. Now, perhaps you better speak to Mr. Domazet. If you come to some agreement about having one or two or something there, then that's a matter between you and then we will just note that it's been done by consent. But we cannot make any ruling upon your objection if you take it at any time other than it's all been unnecessary and it's all irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So perhaps you might like to reconsider your answer to that. Is there nothing upstairs in the OTP which -- in which this has been examined?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm also -- have to prove persecution in this case and it is the position of the Prosecution that many of these events that have been described by these Prosecution witnesses are relevant to the Court's determination of persecution, the campaign against the civilian population of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but what Mr. Domazet is going to prove, how is that relevant to the issue of persecution? Except, as I said to him, does it suggest that there is a motive for retaliation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, if you want to put that, you put it, but for heaven's sake, let's get it on the record somewhere that really is the Prosecution's view.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is not the Prosecution's view, Your Honour. The Prosecution's view is just simply that Mr. Domazet is entitled to present a defence in this case. At this stage, I don't feel that I am in a position to -- to object until I hear some of that evidence. I think he's entitled to present some of it so that the Court has a fair and balanced view of what happened in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So if you call 15 witnesses on the issue of persecution of the Muslims, you feel he should be entitled to call 15 witnesses about persecution of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I guess what I'm saying is that it's up to the Court to determine when it's heard enough of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, it's not. That is totally wrong. It is never the job of a Trial Chamber to say it's heard enough unless it has all been given without any form of issue being taken with the evidence. We can say there has been no objection to two witnesses saying about that, why do you need to proceed? That's not saying we've heard enough except in a very colloquial form we've had enough of all of this. But we are not here to determine when Mr. Domazet has presented enough of material on a totally irrelevant issue. Now, you have got something which, as I have said, is worthy of a Prosecution's indictment. So you are in exactly the same position as an accused person. You know the general nature of the case he wishes to present. You must be able to tell me what your attitude to it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no, no. You must be able to determine what your attitude is. Now, if you haven't formed an attitude yet, I'd like to know why not. I've given you the opportunity. We've said we wanted it in writing. If you want some further time to do that, to consult perhaps some other Prosecution teams to see if they've ever thought of an answer, I would be very grateful. Unfortunately, there never seems to be any communication upstairs between the Prosecution teams and it is very disturbing that we get no real assistance from the accumulated wisdom of the Prosecution office and the number of trials it's done. Surely you have up there all of these research tanks. They must have an index to what they've had to give advice on. Have you consulted any of those to see whether they have ever had to determine what the relevance of this evidence could be?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll seek their advice, Your Honour, and refile tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay. That will be of great assistance to us. Now, the next one. Mr. Domazet, you have filed a response in relation to the 92 bis statements, asking why the Defence can't be present when the witness statements are taken. I fear that you have a misunderstanding of what Rule 92 bis is. There is no formal hearing where the witness in effect gives evidence. There is a formal hearing only to comply with the technicalities of the Rule about identification and the signature and that sort of thing. The purpose of Rule 92 is to save time in having evidence given orally. If the Trial Chamber accepts a statement under Rule 92 bis, it is also in a position to say whether the witness should attend for cross-examination. The Defence loses no right they have to cross-examine the witnesses. But where there is sometimes very detailed evidence about matters that don't directly involve the accused, the object of the Rule is to save the time of that evidence being taken orally. It was, I think, a recognition of the conflict between the civil law system and the common law system, where the civil law system relies almost entirely upon the statements and the Trial Court leads the evidence through his statement, and the common law system, which requires the witness to give his evidence unaided by a written statement. The distinction drawn is between evidence which directly relates to the accused person and evidence which does not, and the idea of the Rule is to save time, that's all. So there's no need for the Defence to be present unless there's going to be some issue as to whether the person who signs the document was, in fact, the person named in it. I don't think there should be any worry about that. But you do not lose your right to have them attend for cross-examination, provided you can demonstrate there is at least some basis upon which you want to cross-examine them. So does that explain to you what this Rule 92 bis procedure is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand why the Defence does not participate. I also had in mind Rule 71, about out of Court records, depositions, at which the Defence does participate, and maybe that would have been better way for some of this testimony. But I wrote this motion because, in my opinion, it is not logical for an investigator of the Prosecution to be present but only the presiding officer, according to the Rule 92 bis. But if that is the Rule, I have to accept, but in any event, it isn't all that important because I understand the purpose of this Rule now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the sinister aspect of having the investigator there. The investigator is probably the person who prepared the statement in collaboration with the witness, but I don't see myself that there's any problem with that. Now, when you say you object to one of these, the first named (redacted) because what he has said in his statement is false, that is the very sort of matter that you can raise in cross-examination. And if you want any of these to attend in cross-examination, you should notify or put a document on stating that you want the particular witnesses to attend for cross-examination with the sort of statement you've made about [redacted] demonstrating that there is an issue you want to cross-examine them on. Now, perhaps you better reassess your attitude towards the Rule 92 bis statements which the Prosecution wants to have accepted. When would you like to give us a fresh assessment of your attitude towards them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not object to the presentation of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis for all proposed witnesses, except for all Witness [redacted] As I have explained in my submission, first of all, I did not receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have got myself into trouble. I had not seen all of the pseudonyms beside it. That will all have to be redacted out of the transcript. Perhaps you should refer to him as Witness 37. I'm sorry, Mr. Domazet, to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was saying, only with respect to Witness 37, I did not receive, attached to the statement, that the statement was taken pursuant to Rule 92 bis, and that is why I feel that that statement cannot be used in accordance with this Rule. However, if the Trial Chamber were to find that it was taken in that manner and no such evidence was provided to me, I objected; that from the attachments produced by that witness, it is evident that he did not speak the truth in part and that for this reason, cross-examination is necessary of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, just what is the situation about each of these six witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, we haven't received Defence's response yet so I wasn't quite aware. There is one mistake that occurred. Actually, number 37 was taken an affidavit according to US procedures. The affidavit, we tried to print it out from the system over the weekend, but unfortunately our system failed us on that, and this is why probably Mr. Domazet objected, because he didn't see the affidavit which was taken according to US procedures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And does it contain the material from his original statement that Mr. Domazet is challenging?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's just a confirmation of his old statement. There was additional information taken relating to another case but which we don't intend to offer into evidence into this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see, it was hoped - and this obviously is something which the Prosecution has some trouble with - it was hoped that there would be proper statements taken from each of the witnesses which deal solely with the material which is relevant to the particular case. If you use the old statement, we are then faced with an enormous amount of material which is irrelevant.
