I'm not criticising anybody when I say that, because I understand that when the statements are taken, nobody has been charged, nobody knows what crimes have been committed, even. So that the investigators take a statement which contains everything the proposed witness wants to say. Very little of it ever gets into evidence. And the intention behind 92 bis would be that there would be fresh statements taken which do deal solely with the relevant material. This hasn't been done here, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: If I may try to respond that. We chose six statements particularly in order to corroborate the evidence given about the persecutorial campaign at the time in 1992 in Visegrad and the build-up of the conflict. We have heard evidence here, and it was suggested that those six statements just confirm, actually, more or less what was given there in evidence, just probably a bit more explained the political and military background at the time in 1992 in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Has there been any attempt to put a line through those parts of the statements upon which the Prosecution is not relying?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: We could endeavour that if this would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's going to be very little, because we already minimised really the amount which we intended to introduce instead of live testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, as I understand him, says he has received nothing by way of Rule 92 bis statements other than the statement that you want to tender them. Now, you better perhaps discuss this with Mr. Domazet, see if you can sort out what has happened. The document which he sent was received by fax on Friday and was actually filed on Friday, so the Prosecution, as I understand it, would have been notified there are documents to pick up. So there must be a copy there for you. But if you need another copy, we'll get one for you, but you better sort out with Mr. Domazet what it is that he has to deal with and perhaps, if you can, what the Trial Chamber should do about it because we are a little alarmed at the thought that we are going to have a lot of material before us which is irrelevant. All right. Well, we'll deal with the other two matters, or three, I think there are, when we return at 11.30. We'll adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, one suggestion that you may like to consider about this irrelevant material is that it goes in in some written form, then you have some control over what is going to happen. Now the next one is your request for a subpoena in relation to the mother and son. Why do you think that that is something which your investigators or whoever have been unable to do this is to persuade them to come? The threat of making them guilty of contempt does not seem to get us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. We're not getting any transcript. We are now. Thank you. I think we've lost a fair bit of it, but hopefully it will be in the transcript at the end of the day. Now, why do you think that this subpoena will do something which the persuasion doesn't?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that it will. I feel it is incumbent upon me, especially since so many of the other witnesses have assumed these risks and have come to the Tribunal to testify that I pursue every possible option. Most recently we had contacted another son who is in law enforcement of the witness and it seemed that we had overcome these fears and we even offered to have that particular son accompany the witness. We were advised late Thursday or sometime on Thursday that the decision was taken again not to come. As I say, Your Honour, I don't have any basis for believing that we will be successful. I hope that we will, and I believe it is my duty and responsibility at this stage to pursue every legal means to try to secure the presence of these two witnesses before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it looks to me under Rule 54 rather under the Trial Chamber I assume, is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. I'll sign one, but you better provide one of the legal officers with a floppy disk with it on so it doesn't have to be retyped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, the expert reports. There are two applications. Dr. Clark appears on them twice. I'm not quite sure why that is so. There's one dated the 11th of September, which includes his report, and another one of the 12th of September which includes his report or are they different reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Ossogo will deal with the issues related to Mr. Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. I haven't checked them, Mr. Ossogo, to see whether they're the same but I assume they are, are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. That is to say they're not completely identical. The first report is dated the 5th of September. It was an incomplete report, but we thought it would be useful to communicate it to the Defence within this time limit and five days later we received a complete report which contained a photograph, the exhumation site, and we said to the Registry that this 17th of September report would be replacing -- taking the place of the 5th of September report. So it is the -- this report that we are handing over to the Defence for it to be able to tell us if it is in accord or not in keeping with Rule 94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the first we've heard that one is intended to replace the other, but now that you've said that it makes sense. And you are providing the Defence with the incomplete report just as a matter of history. You also want to add his name to the list of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Mr. Domazet, what is your attitude -- I'm sorry, is there something you wanted to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's right Mr. President, yes. I have nothing to add thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, what is your attitude to this application to add Dr. Clark as an additional expert witness? The explanation that was given was that his availability was not certain at the time the pre-trial brief was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Ossogo, I don't know if you received a motion, my motion dated the 15th of September. That was sent by fax. It was faxed to you. And the Defence states its views in that motion. I can explain it now. With respect to Rule 94 bis (A) to have the time -- Rule 94 bis (A) is what I'm referring to, and it states a period of 21 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you would find it easier to speak in the B/C/S, please do so. We're very envious of your ability to speak French, but it is obviously, I think, more difficult for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In this motion, and we said that the Defence received on the 7th and on the 9th of September written findings, and we consider that the time limit stipulated in Rule 94 bis (ii) should be adhered to and also the 14 days period within Rule 94 bis (B) with respect to stating whether we wish to cross-examine the expert witness or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, whether or not we stick completely to the Rules of that nature is a matter we can discuss later on. I really don't think that the Prosecution should be denied calling a valid witness simply because it might be one day short of the time unless there is some real prejudice from the accused's point of view. But let's leave that to one side. My first question to you was: What do you want to say about adding this witness to the witness list? That doesn't rely on 94 bis. That's in relation to the pre-trial brief, where the Prosecution is required to set out the witnesses it proposes to call. It did not put Mr. Clark's name on that list because, it is explained, his availability was uncertain at that time. Now, do you object to his name being added to the witness list, first of all? How he gives his evidence will be another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, I have no objection to make to Dr. John Clark, the witness testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, now, you will have 14 days from the delivery of this to you in which to put your response on. When is it proposed to call this witness, Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the week of the 1st of October, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My maths is never the best when you go over a month, but when was the document -- when was the statement served on the Defence? 12th of September. Yes, you're in time. All right. Well, thank you for that. Mr. Domazet, if you can give us an answer before 14 days that would be to everybody's benefit, but you have 14 days to reply in response to the expert evidence that they wish to call. Well, those are the only matters that I have listed. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's a scheduling matter I'd like to bring to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, for several reasons this trial is moving at a faster pace than anticipated, in part or a large part rescheduling by the Registry. It's only last week that we learned that we would have additional sessions this week that we didn't anticipate last week. I just want to bring to the Court's attention, we've endeavoured to bring -- we actually 12 witnesses here this week to put before the Tribunal. I just want to make the Court aware that we have encountered some problems securing visas from the Dutch government to have these witnesses enter the country. Nearly all of the witnesses are coming from abroad. So there are no immediate problems. I just wanted to bring to the Court's attention that there may be some problems in the coming days and the following week regarding being able to have sufficient witnesses present. We are still endeavouring to do our best. I can assure the Court, though, that we still anticipate completing the Prosecution case at least a week or possibly two weeks prior than our original estimation. I have a schedule, as best we're able to tell at this stage, Your Honour, of the entire prosecution case, and if the Court wishes, I'd just like to tender that to the Court at this stage. It goes beyond -- what you have just been handed, Your Honour, is just this week. I propose to give you our schedule for the entire case which it looks like that we would complete our case on the 1st or 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, yes. But you keep referring to this change. There has been very little change. There is a difference between sitting for four hours a day or, I think it's five minutes short of four hours a day to four and a half hours a day. That's the only difference. So I really hope we don't have that explanation put up to us again. What we are very grateful for is that the case is moving more quickly, as indeed it should have been anticipated that it would, but nevertheless, we accept that you have to re-estimate. We accept that there are problems with getting visas because of the notice that has to be given. If you run out of witnesses at some stage, I can assure you we all have an awful lot to do out of court, and we will spend a very productive time out of court. We would like some notice, though, of when you think you will run out of witnesses so that we can make arrangements, if necessary, for -- at least this is from my own point of view, hearings in other pre-trial matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I propose to provide the Court with the entire schedule for the Prosecution case, and I will communicate both with your legal officer and with Mr. Domazet and keep you up-to-date regarding any changes in the availability of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, well, you may have to give us various versions of this as we proceed. It may move up or it may move down as the case may be. But we do hope, for example, that if you can, you can give us the whole of a Friday off if you are running out of witnesses, because that allows us to list things, or at least allows me to list pre-trial matters in three or four other cases at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this week, all of the witnesses will be in the building as of from Wednesday on, so we will have witnesses to work full time, hopefully, up until whatever time on Thursday their testimony is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. All right then. Well, thank you very much for that. This sort of thing is always a great help to us. Now, your next witness. With this witness, still no protective measures are required, the next one?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's VG55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. The one ahead of that on the list. 55 is number 2 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We provided Friday morning an update, and I think that VG55 was advanced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, dear. Yes. Well, something happened down in the Registry about that, I'm afraid. Are they otherwise in the same order? Perhaps we'll get one later on today if we could. Yes. Very well. 55. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is VG55 the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes. I might ask that the oath be read out to the witness. The witness said she forgot her glasses and she can't read. So it would be good to get that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is VG55 here? It will be necessary to read the solemn declaration to the witness because she does not have her glasses. Thank you. I don't know. It will have to be read into English and translated for her, I should think, unless our court usher has a talent I am unaware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you stand up, please, madam. The usher will read to you the solemn declaration that you will be asked to agree with. After it has been read to you, I will ask you, do you make that solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will always speak the truth, the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You make the declaration in the terms which were read to you by the usher, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I agree with that and will always agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sit down, please, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Witness, you have been assigned the pseudonym VG55 for purposes of concealing your identity, and that is how you will be addressed throughout the proceedings. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You will be handed a piece of paper which contains your name. Could you just say yes or no that it contains your name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately, it will have to be read to her.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You are able to see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you, VG55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, how is the witness going to deal with the rest of the document, Ms. Bauer?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would have hoped that she's going to refer to -- that's why I have put it in the Bosnian language. The print is very large, as you can see, so I hoped she could read the Bosnian term of this paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you better ask her whether she's able to and then explain to her that when she refers, or wants to refer to those three persons, she should refer to them in the way you've described.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown the same piece of paper again and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: She should have her own copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You will have this sheet of paper in front of you. So any time you refer to any of those three names, please just refer in Bosnian to either your brother-in-law, your sister-in-law, or your father-in-law. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And is that the date upon which you were born - or you believe you were born - on the third line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P74, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can it please be left with the witness, open. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: VG55, in 1992, did you live with your late husband and your two children in the village of Musici in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I would like you to recall an incident that happened in the end of March in your village, when Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic came to your house. Where did you know Mitar Vasiljevic for -- from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him when we went to school together. We were friends. We went to school together.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What else did you know about Mitar Vasiljevic's personal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know anything special until it happened, but when we were friends, I didn't know anything bad about him. I can't say I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Do you know what his profession was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes; he was a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where was he a waiter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: In Panos, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you know anybody else of his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I did; I knew his sisters and his wife Milojka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of the conflict, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic several times, once, twice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Before 1992. Before we come to the incident we're going to talk about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I would see him around before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: That evening, how did Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: They came as dusk was falling, Mitar Vasiljevic, and Lukic, Milan Lukic. And there were five or six other people. They stormed my father-in-law's house. Mitar stood in front of the door. And when I went outside the house I said to Mitar, "How's Milojka?" I just didn't want him to kill me, that's all I was thinking of at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said they arrived. Do you know in what kind of car or what kind of colour of car they arrived in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Red, red.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said you were afraid that he would kill you. How was Mitar Vasiljevic dressed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He had black trousers on. I don't know what he had above that. All I know is that he was armed; he had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I don't really know. He was holding a rifle and the rifle was cocked. I don't know. That's all I know. And he was pointing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where did exactly Mitar Vasiljevic stand throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He was standing in front of my door, at the steps to the first entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything when he came, about the reasons why they came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything. When I asked him, "How's Milojka," because I was afraid that he would kill me, all he said was, "She's fine." He didn't say anything else. He didn't say anything to me any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Milan Lukic went into my house. He was armed. He raised his bayonet and turned over the sofas and everything, and he seemed to be looking for some people in my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were you at that time told what the people were looking for or who the people were looking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: They were looking for people. They thought someone was hiding there, and they were looking for people to see if they were hiding there then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were you told this by anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: They said Milan Lukic was looking for some people. He thought that we were harbouring some people, hiding some people in our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: If you say "they," who do you refer to, VG55?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, did he have a ribbon on his gear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He had a red ribbon on his shoulder, on his clothing, a red ribbon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did he wear any headgear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did Milan -- did Mitar Vasiljevic at any time tell you not to worry because you were school buddies and nothing would happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He didn't say anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to anybody else; to your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I didn't hear him say anything to my husband. I didn't hear him say anything to my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was he at all times in front of the house or in the doorstep of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: All the time while Lukic was in the house, he said that nobody should go anywhere out of the village of Musici.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: My question was: Did Mitar Vasiljevic stand the whole time in front of the house or in the doorway of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: In front of the house. At the entrance to the house, on the steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where was he pointing his rifle to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: The sky.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said there were other people with him. Was one of the people a blonde woman at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I didn't see her that evening. I saw her on another occasion but not that night. I just saw five or six other people and they went to my brother-in-law's house and my sister-in-law's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Could you discern from their accents where they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Well, they seemed to be from Serbia. They weren't our people, the ones that went off to my brother-in-law's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic has searched the house, what did he tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He told us to round up our neighbours and that they should all come to my house and that we should tell them to come to my house so that he could give them a piece of advice.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The people all came. There were a lot of people there, women as well, and he told us that we weren't to go anywhere, that we would be safe there. And he hit one man called Suljo on his shoulder, but he said that not a hair of our heads would be harmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did he take anything from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He didn't take anything from my house but he did from my brother-in-law's house. The five or six people that went there, they took money, cigarettes, and some drinks, bottles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: The next day, did Milan Lukic return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No, he didn't return, but the next evening he did return and took seven of our menfolk away in a car.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you see how they were taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Well, I heard the women crying and saying, "Lukic has taken away the seven men." I know those men. They are all my neighbours. And he took them off in a direction and I don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Can you recall the names of those seven men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Can you please list them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, I can: Mustafa Vila, and Nermin Vila, and Suljo Vila, and Uzeir Vila, Vatres -- Vatres, what was the first name? [redacted] [redacted] but the Vatres man, I can't remember his name. Yes, Adil. Adil Vatres and Kasim Murtic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were those men ever seen again after this date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What happened to your father-in-law that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: My father-in-law went towards Prelovo to grind his grain, and he was never seen or heard of again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did the same evening another group come to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, another group came, and they took us to another house. There was this ploughshare, and there were some other people in the village, and they led us to another house to gather us in that other house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Who was the leader of this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: That was a blonde lady. She kept pushing me with her rifle in the back, and I was asking her, "Where are we going?" And she said, "I didn't ask you anything." She just kept pushing me in the back with her rifle to make me go faster.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was she a local or was she from another country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: She wasn't a local. She had a strange accent when she spoke. She spoke Serbian dialect.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did she do to you when you assembled with the other villagers in the other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: When we assembled in front of a house, they were waiting there. There was another group of men, and one of them came up to me, and he asked me, "Who did you vote for? Did you vote for Alija?" I kept quiet and didn't say anything. They assembled us there and asked us, "What is the name of this village?" And I said, "Musici." And he said, "You'll see what Musici is."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did he mean, "You will see what Musici is"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How can she possibly answer that? What did she understand him to mean might be a different question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Well, it is a Bosnian translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did he say to you Mutici or Musici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I said "Musici," and she said, "It will now be Mutici," Mutici meaning suffering.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when they robbed all our money and valuables?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. They waited for Milan Lukic, because he had taken away the men, and they were waiting for him to come. And they forced us into this house and they said give us whatever jewellery and money you have. I took off my jewellery, threw it on the floor, and the people who had money, they put it down there and then Milan came back. They collected it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When Milan came back, what did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: When he came back, he first asked, "Where is the man whose house we were in yesterday?" And that was my father-in-law's house, and that is what he asked us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What else did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Then he said that we should go inside, and he asked whether anyone had fuel, that we should move to the stable. I suppose he wanted to start a fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: They stood in front of the door, and they were sort of drawing lots to see what they would do to us. Then he came back to the house and said, "We won't do anything to you. But another group may come to do something to you." But then he said, "Go to your own houses, but don't stay in them. Go where you want."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What happened to your husband and your brother-in-law that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Then he said, "You and you, come with us, and the rest of you go back to where you came from." Then I and my sister-in-law started pleading with them, "Leave our men." And then he said, "We'll just interrogate them and then we'll bring them back."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: With "you and you," do you refer to your husband and your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, my husband and his brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: The next day, did you and your sister-in-law go to find your husbands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I spent the night in the basement with my children. In the morning, we got up. We caught a bus that was passing through our village. We took the bus, and there were other women with us, my sister-in-law, and we went to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where exactly in Visegrad did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: We went in the direction of the MUP, the police in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there a time when Milan Lukic came to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. There were people working there in the MUP, and they asked us what we wanted, and we said we were looking for our husbands. They said, "Who took them away?" And we said, "Lukic." And the man said, "Wait until he comes," and then Lukic came. We waited and he came.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did he tell you when you asked for your husbands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: A man said to him, "These women are waiting, inquiring about their husbands." And he said, "Fuck them." That's what he said to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you went back to your village and your sister-in-law continued to search for your two husbands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Later that day, did your sister-in-law come back and tell you what would be the destiny of your husbands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: She said, "Our husbands are coming." And I said, "That's not possible." And a little while later our husbands did come to our village of Musici.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Who accompanied them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I know that Lukic, Sredoje, he brought them in a car. There was another man, and I'm afraid I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Who was Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He was a neighbour of mine. I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What was his profession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did he tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He said -- we went to my sister-in-law's house when our men came, and we thanked him for bringing our husbands. And he told us that we couldn't stay there any longer, that this would be Serbia, and that we should go and join our own people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did your sister-in-law or did he tell you why he released your husband and his brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He said that my sister-in-law had deserved it because she had helped him when he was building his house and that it was because of her that he had brought back my husband and my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was this help in any way monetary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there a day when a number of young Serbs came to your village asking for a sheep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: How did they approach you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I was close by. They came in a car, young men. They had big crosses round their necks, and they cursed the mosque and faith of my neighbour. And when I came up to her, she said, "They're looking for a sheep." I said, "Would a young cow do?" And they said, "No, only a sheep."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were those Serbs from Serbia or local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Serbs from Serbia. They were not from our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was that the same day when you were on your way with Jasmina Vila, when you met Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do with Jasmina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: We took the sheep down. They put it in the car, and then Lukic said, "You must report to me," and the girl left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did she come back the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three hours later, she returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What was her condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did she look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: She was blue under the eyes, and she was wet. Her clothes were wet on top, and she tied a sweater around her waist.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did she tell you what had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: She said that he had done whatever he wanted, that is, he raped her, and that he had said that we mustn't stay there, that we would all be slaughtered, and that we must go our own way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was that the night your husbands decided to swim across the river and leave the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: That evening, our husbands crossed the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were you a few days later told by local Serbs to leave the area because you would all be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you gather a few things and leave for Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you try to get into a convoy of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: We did, but they were saying, "No one will take you," and we returned. We didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: They -- if you refer to "they," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I mean the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: On your way there, did you meet some paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: On your way to Visegrad and to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No. When we were going to the convoy, they would assemble, and they had knives, and they would play around with these knives, and they would throw bread at us, and they were teasing us and treating us like dogs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did they threaten you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No, not really. They were provoking us. They were always armed. They were unpleasant towards us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did they say what they would do with your children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: When we reached the Red Cross, they said that they would first slaughter our children for us, that we would watch them do, and then they would do the same to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you went into hiding in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: In a Muslim house in Lipe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When you left it, the house, why did you flee from the house? Can you describe the incident, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I can. We fled because there were four murders in that house. They killed four women, and myself and my sister-in-law threw our children out of the window to save ourselves and that is how we fled that night.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: One last question: Would you be able today to recognise Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Do you see him somewhere in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the record where he is sitting, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He's sitting in the last seat up there from the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Can you describe basically what he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: A suit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Which colour? Do you see the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He has a white shirt and a red tie. A black tie, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, that evening when Milan Lukic came for the first time or, rather, when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic with him, you explained that you were rather scared.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did any one of those persons, on that particular occasion, threaten you, or more specifically, did Mitar Vasiljevic threaten you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: No. He didn't say anything to me and he didn't threaten me, only what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic threaten, apart from what you told us he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: He didn't threaten me at all. He just said that we were safe there, that we shouldn't go anywhere that evening. That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you said, madam, that you remember that Mitar was wearing a red ribbon, can you remember whether it was a ribbon round one of his sleeves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was round his sleeve after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it a wide ribbon or a narrow ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: A narrow ribbon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you notice anything on it, on the ribbon itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Just the red colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember when that incident occurred, roughly which month? Because I think that in the transcript, the month indicated was not mentioned, even in your first statement. So it might just be an error. It says March. Was it March or May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I think it was May, the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you think it was the end of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes, the end of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Domazet, we're running into the usual problem. Madam, because you and Mr. Domazet, the counsel here, are speaking the same language, it is difficult for the interpreters to keep up with you both unless there is a pause before you answer the question. Mr. Domazet will have to pause before he asks the question. If you'd just give us a brief moment whilst the interpreters translate into English and into French for us, then you answer the question. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You told us when this incident occurred for the first time, but today you also described the second incident. But could you tell us how much time passed between the two? Was it one day or two days later or a little longer when the second incident occurred that you described, when the seven were taken from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: They weren't taken away that night, but another day, seven men were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. That is how I understood you the first time. But was it the very next day or two or more days later, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: The next evening immediately, seven men were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So the next day. And this group with the blonde lady came that same evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes. That same evening, this woman assembled us down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you were describing the event after which all of you who were in the village headed for the Red Cross in Visegrad, you said that a group of local Serbs came. Could you tell me from which village they came and who they were, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I don't know those people, but I would see them. I don't know their names. I know they are from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are they from Visegrad or the village of Greben, which is close to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I think there were more from Visegrad than from Greben. I didn't recognise anyone from Greben among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that on that day, at the Red Cross in Visegrad, while you were waiting, a group of men in uniform threatened you and provoked you in various ways. Could you judge by their accent whether they were local Serbs from Visegrad or people from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: There were some Visegrad and some from Serbia. It was a mixed group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you said today that the reason for your leaving Bikavac was four murders, could you please tell us, if you can remember, who carried out those murders? Who were the murderers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't see them. If I had seen them, I probably wouldn't be alive. I just know the names of the women who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you don't know or you cannot remember the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I don't remember who did the killing. I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Bauer, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Only one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Witness VG55, when Mitar Vasiljevic was there that night, he didn't threaten you, but how did you feel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: I was a little scared that he might kill him, and I addressed him by name so that he would recognise him and that he wouldn't kill me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, for coming here to give evidence. Thank you for the evidence which you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You better tell us, Mr. Groome, who the next witness is. We haven't got the revised list yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness, Your Honour, Witness VG116.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is this a person who has got the pseudonym since the list was typed?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honour, unless there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There's no 116, even on the most recent edition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the one that was handed out this morning on the 11.30 to 1.00 session it is VG116?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the third edition of the list, is it? We have one here dated the 13th of September, another one dated the 14th of September. And there's now one dated the 17th of September, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour the most recent one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As you can understand, we are a little at a loss.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There has been a struggle to get these witnesses into the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I understand all of that. I'm just trying to see that we are all operating from the same document. Oh, you mean the schematic one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, we have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a protected witness, and I'm going to -- the first thing I'm going to ask him to do is look at a video in which he appears. So could I ask that we begin in private session and then after he views the video, we'll come out of private session and he can discuss the video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we better get him -- I was going to say sworn in, but at least settled in and then we'll into a private session, yes. This was a pseudonym that we gave at the beginning of the trial. I can go through and look at the transcript, but it's not on the pseudonym list, unfortunately. Oh, here we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just to avoid any confusion, Your Honour, the larger print is a witness that this witness may possibly refer to. I made it large because of some problems he has with seeing. That's the reference to VG22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The witness is temporarily delayed, but we'll wait for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting, I'd also ask that the oath be read to the witness. Again, he has problems with his vision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: While we're waiting, I see we've got Dr. de Grave on Wednesday. Whoever speaks to him beforehand, would they please ask him, and I give a tremendous amount of emphasis to this, that he speak in other than the Latin language? He's one of those doctors who understandably speaks in a language which he understands, but it really is very difficult. Unless we have a medical dictionary besides us, it's hard to follow him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll convey that to him this evening, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you stand up, please, sir. Now, the usher will read to you the solemn oath, and once he's read that, I will ask you do you make that solemn declaration, I'm sorry -- do you make that declaration? THE USHER: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you make that declaration, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG55
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet will be Exhibit P75 and it is under seal. Yes, Mr. Groome. Tell us when you want to go into private session, but get his details first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. 116.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd just like you to explain to us briefly where you were born and what was your occupation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I was born in the village of [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Visegrad, yes. A village near Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you born on the [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your occupation when you were working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I'm a [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's a glass of water there on the table. Feel free to take a drink whenever you need one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be shown a video, but before we do that, I'm going to ask that we go into private session for the showing of that videotape.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. 116, we are now in public session, so I would ask you to refer to your sons, if you have to, just as your sons and not use their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want you to describe for the Court how it was that you came to be in that truck.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, when the corps entered the town, a lot of people came from Dobrun, fled from the corps, from Dobrun, and we took to the woods, all of us. All the people fled to the woods. And the people were very scared. They didn't know what to do, and went down to the road. I went back home to my own village to see to the livestock, to let them out, because I didn't know if I would return alive. So I had to let the livestock out. So when I let the cattle out, I went along the road. I was all alone, roaming around. There was nobody there. And I didn't know what to do or where to go. And then from down there there was the army, and there were trucks, and there were lots of people in the trucks, both in the truck and behind the truck. Next to me they were passing by me, and a soldier was there and he said, "Old man, get up onto -- into the vehicle." And I jumped up, of course, and I went with them wherever they were going. I jumped up onto the car. When I jumped up onto the car there was the army, and there were two women and a child. I didn't ask who they were, but they were sitting next to my son. I tried to talk to the soldiers a little bit but they didn't want to talk to me. They didn't want to talk to us at all. And then we went off into town, this whole column. There were big cars and small cars. And I thought, well, let's go into town, come what may. We'll see. Then when we crossed the bridge, on this one side there were lots of people, and they were painted on their heads and had stockings, and they went to a cafe. There were lots of people there, all different people wearing different clothing. There was civilians and policemen and people wearing military uniforms as well. I turned my head to take a look, and I said -- some of them were cursing our balija mothers. Others were saying, "We'll slaughter you." And I complained to one of the soldiers, whether they would take us down from the car. And he laughed and said, "There wouldn't be anything" -- "What would be wrong with that?" So I looked to see if there was anybody I recognised, whom I knew. When we moved towards the station, went through town, a man was crying. He was crying and moaning, said, "They took me down from the truck, and he said, "[redacted], my son, brothers, help me. What am I going to do?" He was crying, going up and -- walking up and down. I didn't dare ask the soldiers to help the people, because they would see where is -- they would say, "Where is Musan [redacted]. And when we reached the station, on the -- down below there was the stadium where the football matches are, and they had all guns, young soldiers, and one of them said, "Let's go and search all the houses up there to see if there are any balijas in them." And I said to him, "Why take us now?" Well, he said, "We're taking you down there now. Later on you're not going anywhere." I found so many people down there. They were all quiet, with their big bags and bundles. Nobody said a word. And then somebody said, "Here comes the commander in a helicopter." And I sort of hid a little bit. The commander arrived. Lots people gathered round him, and some other people too, and the army, the soldiers were holding their guns, pointing them upwards to the sky. They didn't talk to anybody. Then they positioned two soldiers in the centre, and every man and woman had to pass by them, these soldiers, and they searched the people passing by, as they passed by. When that was done, some other people came up to him. I think his name was Ojdanic. They referred to him as Ojdanic, and they said, "Well, we'll go home. What are we going to do with them in the camp?" And he said, "Who is from Musici and the nearby villages Jelacici and so forth. They can go back home. We've liberated that." Well, there's nobody to liberate it from. It's only the people, the inhabitants, no army at all. But anyway we went off, and we went through town hiding. There were two bridges. Some of us took the lower bridge, others took the upper bridge, and we tried to avoid being caught. We were afraid. And we arrived home. What happened to the others who stayed on, I don't know. I don't know when they were released or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. 116, I'd ask you to take a drink and water, and I'm going to ask you a few specific questions earlier on in your account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I remind you that he should not name his son? And he also named either himself or -- yes, himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Himself. We've handed up the redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we've picked them up, but it's very difficult.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. 116, I know that it's difficult. This is kind of an artificial set of circumstances we work under, but to the extent you're able, try not to refer to names or other identifying facts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to take you back to where you -- to the point in time where you describe first seeing these army trucks. Were they JNA -- were they Yugoslav People's Army trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you saw -- said that you saw many. Can you give us your best idea regarding approximately how many of these army trucks you saw --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Lots.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- at that time? And was this on a road leading --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I can't say, but on the road, a large column, lots of trucks. They were full, and there were soldiers, too, all young soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was this on one of the roads leading into Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that in the preceding days to this event, you had been hiding in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when you first saw the trucks, did you see your son on one of those trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the soldiers that you mentioned, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes. Each one of them was armed with an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the truck that you saw that your son was riding in, were there soldiers on that truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: All soldiers, yes, young soldiers. I know what the -- what an army is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified that somebody called out to you and instructed you to get on the truck. Can you tell us exactly what was said to you as best you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, he said, "Old man, get up onto the truck." He sort of screamed at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And he was one of the soldiers in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a soldier, not a civilian. None of them were civilians. And my son didn't even dare say a word. Nobody dared say a word. The soldiers were very angry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that this incident you're describing for us now occurred on the left bank or the western side of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, on the left-hand side if you go downstream to the Drina. Ustipraca, my village, and the right bank is the other side. So left -- on the left-hand side of the town as you go downstream, down the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, which of the two bridges or did this truck cross one of the bridges into Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: They all crossed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And which bridge did the truck that you were riding in cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: The old bridge up there, the first as you come in from Ustipraca. The old bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that the entire bridge was filled with army trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In addition to carrying people on the trucks, did some of these trucks also carry artillery equipment and other military equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Those same trucks carried the artillery which was joined to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, of the civilians that you saw on these trucks, of those civilians that you recognised, were they all Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any people of Serb ethnicity that were civilians on these trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say, but no, no, there wasn't a single Serb there, just Muslims from my villages, the villages around my own village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, as the truck that you were riding in reached the end of the bridge, the end of the bridge on the right bank of the river, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: On the left-hand side. On the left. On the left side, there was a garden and poplars, poplar trees. And people were standing there masked. They had soot on their faces, paint on them, with some stockings, and you could just see the eyes. But we were a big column. I didn't dare look too much, because the soldier would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, these men that you saw, they were on the right bank of the river; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We crossed the bridge on our side, and we crossed the bridge and the left-hand side, I come to the right side, and then we passed by the poplars. The bridge is straight ahead to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you're indicating that these men were standing to the left of the bridge as you left the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: When you cross the Drina River and want to go into town, then it's to the left in town. I come into town, and we're moving towards the station through town, and the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar where the Hotel Visegrad is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I do know, yes. I know Hotel Visegrad. It's just when you cross the bridge on the left-hand side, a new hotel. And that's where they were lined up, right down this small street, all lined up. And they cursed us, swore at us. And we took the road, the upper road into town, moving towards the station the column was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, the ones that were standing down there, well, they sworn our balija mothers, cursed our balija mothers, and they said, "You won't last long. We'll slaughter you. We'll slit your throats." And I thought they would take me down on the truck, but we passed by somehow, by the stadium somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you were able to hear this clearly from where you were sitting in the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, yes. It wasn't two metres away from them, from where they were standing right by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would the soldiers on the truck have been in a position to have heard these threats as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, of course they were able to hear. And they were laughing. They laughed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you at any time hear or see any of the soldiers do anything or take any action to stop these threats against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, nobody lifted a finger. They just looked at us --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These men that you're describing as having their faces --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: -- devouring us with their eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These men that you're describing as having their faces disguised, as best you're able, can you approximate how many there were for the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Well, as far as I was able to see, some 50 metres off along the road on the left they were lined up, right along the road, all along the road. There was a lot of them. I can't tell you exactly, I didn't count them, but lots.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when your truck, put the people on your truck to the bus station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did this truck eventually carry you to the bus station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The whole column arrived at the station and all the people in it arrived at the station, on the truck and in the little cars. Everybody left in big cars, small cars. They had to, because we thought that somebody would protect us. But that wasn't the case. As far as I was able to see, nobody tried to do anything in contravention to these soldiers, the young soldiers, to protect anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In fact, you described for the Court seeing somebody standing at the side of the road that you recognised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: You mean on the left-hand side, among those people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You referred to a person crying. That's the person I'm referring to now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see a person crying by the side of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: When we started off and passed the people, the station, there was a man crying, jumping up and down, coming up to our truck, and as far as he I remember, he said, "They took my son from the -- [redacted] from the truck, Musan Smajic. They took them from my car. They took my son from my car, Musan Smajic."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who did you understand him to be referring to when he said "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't find him and ask him actually what happened, but he was just crying and jumping up and down. And I'm sorry that I didn't actually ask him more. But he never saw his son again. From that day onwards, never again. So he should tell you. He should tell you what actually happened and who had taken his son, seized his son. He must know who took his son away. He must recognise someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now take you to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it might be a good idea if you came back to it after lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 2.30. The -- there are a few confusions as to whether or not he's referring to his son or to somebody else's son in that evidence. We've just redacted something which I think actually was not meant to be his son, but it is very confusing. We'll come back to it, sir, later. Thank you. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I resume, I'd just like to correct a few bookkeeping matters regarding an exhibit referred to earlier on today, and the video that was shown, referred to as Prosecution number 142, I'm going to propose that it be called 142.1. And, Your Honour, I will not be tendering it at this time. I will need to establish some foundational facts regarding other portions of the video with another witness, but I have turned it over to the custody of the registrar, and it will remain there until this other witness testifies. Your Honour, by agreement with Defence counsel, Mr. Domazet, I would propose to tender Exhibit number 142.2, and that is a video capture of the key portion of that, and I would move to tender that under seal as it does reveal the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this does that, but just in case, certainly. There's no objection to this -- what did you call it, a video capture?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: A still photograph taken from the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I have to objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P142.2 and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one other minor matter, Your Honour. The other day, a witness made markings on P131 and P133 and they made those markings in highlighter. Unfortunately that highlighter cannot be reproduced if it is photocopied. By agreement with Defence counsel, we have authorised to have the registrar retrace that highlighted markings with some type of pen that will allow it to be pre-produced for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Hopefully a black one. Yes, I remember them well. Very well, we'll get the court deputy on to that in her spare time, if she has any. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. 116, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just before lunch, you were referring to a person who was telling you something about his son. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, the son that we're referring to is his son and not your own son; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, his son. His son. He was standing by the car, close to the station, when the column started moving. Musan Smajic was his name, and he was crying out, "They took my son away." I don't know whether it was from the truck or from a car. And he stayed behind crying, as we went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at the bus station, approximately how many Muslims --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: When we were on our way to the bus station, at a bend in the road in the centre of town this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at the bus station, were there other Muslims present at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes. Almost the whole stadium was almost full. I don't know when they had got there. I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm asking you now before you arrive at the stadium, but at the time that you arrive at the bus station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it true that other Muslims --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Before. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it true that other Muslims, like yourself, arrived in army trucks at the bus station as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know about the trucks coming from our villages carrying Muslims. They had probably brought some before, but I didn't ask, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At some point later on in this day, did you go to the football stadium in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I didn't go there. I didn't dare go into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you go to some football stadium in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I did go when they took us there that day, but not after that. Later -- not later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where in town or where in Visegrad is this football stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: At the railway station. This was later -- the bus station as well, but to the left of that station was where the stadium was built for football matches, and that is where they took us. And the whole stadium was almost packed full with people. There were women and children as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate for the Court how many Muslims were gathered in that stadium that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I wouldn't dare make an estimate, but from all the surrounding villages and from the right bank of the river and from the left bank of the Drina, I recognised people there, but how they got there, I didn't ask. Those villages are quite far away from town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there soldiers from the Yugoslav People's Army there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes, of course. They held their rifles pointing upwards. The people were scared. Then this man in the helicopter arrived. The soldiers approached him. They called him Ojdanic. And they talked and talked about us, and then they selected two soldiers to stand one next to another so that each person had to pass between the two of them so as to be searched. What they were looking for, weapons or what, I don't know. And when all this was over, darkness was approaching, and the people from my villages asked to go home. And he said, "As Musici are close by to town and to the let of my village, (redacted)," and he said, "Those two villages have been liberated so you may go home." So each one of us went his own way, finding his path through town so as to avoid being caught by those people with paint on their faces and socks over their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you see those same people as you left town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I did see them walking around town. They had scattered. They were no longer lined up, and they walked around town later on. There were a lot of them. And we, all of us, hid out of town so as to avoid being caught. We wanted to get home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did they say anything to you or the people around you when you tried to leave town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I can't say that, because -- because I took a winding path. I was all alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I'm just going to ask that the large Exhibit 17.1, it's the large overview shot of Visegrad, just be set up for a few minutes so that the witness can indicate some of the places he's referred to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: I can when you show me that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, there is a problem. Well, the simplest way will be to go into private session, because if he stands up, he loses the facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. We'll go into private session then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. 116, after you returned to your home, did there come a time when a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- a person by the name of Captain Bunardic arrived at your house with a list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG116
utterances.text: No. He came -- Pavle, Pavle Bunardic. He was the commander. And when the soldiers came, there were the houses, Crnici over there, from the direction I came along, and they were sitting there with my neighbours and brothers.
